{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABahjyPA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEIB9A", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 8, "title": "Compile user-edited Verilog entirely in the browser", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL's GitHub Pages demo currently runs only a **precompiled** counter. Editing RTL in the published site cannot change the running circuit, because the existing Verilator -> C++ -> Emscripten -> WebAssembly compilation flow runs outside the browser (locally or during deployment).

The next milestone is to **compile user-edited Verilog and run the resulting circuit entirely inside the browser**, without a compilation API, local server, or GitHub Actions build for each edit.

## Expected outcome

On the static WebRTL site (GitHub Pages), a user can modify the supplied counter's Verilog, click **Compile**, and execute the **newly compiled design** with Run / Pause / Step / Reset. All compilation and simulation execution must happen client-side.

The toolchain itself may be prebuilt and distributed as static WASM/JS assets. A browser-side compiler worker can use Verilator and a WebAssembly-capable C++ compiler/linker, or an alternative approach if it preserves the intended functionality. Evaluate existing OSS (e.g. Vera/YoWASP and associated toolchains) before adding a custom compiler.

## Proposed scope

- Run the HDL compilation pipeline **inside the browser**, using a Web Worker or equivalent isolation to keep the UI responsive.
- Start from the existing counter interface and prove recompilation with meaningful RTL edits, such as changing the increment from 1 to 3.
- Produce and load an executable browser simulation from the newly compiled design; do not emulate the counter in JavaScript or substitute a prebuilt design regardless of edits.
- Preserve Run / Pause / Step / Reset, and show compiler diagnostics/progress/errors.
- Maintain a clear boundary between project source files, compiler/toolchain, generated simulator, and UI so the design can evolve toward an IDE and additional modules.
- Keep GitHub Pages deployable as static assets. GitHub Actions may build **the application and browser-hosted compiler tools**, but must not compile each user's HDL design.
- Document supported browsers, supported HDL features, loading/compilation performance, memory constraints, and the architecture.

### Multiple-file projects

Multi-file RTL designs and top-module selection are an important **follow-up capability**. Avoid architectural assumptions that prevent adding them (e.g. a hardcoded counter-only compiler), but do not require a full file explorer, project management UI, or general multi-file support to complete this first browser-compilation milestone.

## Out of scope

- Full FPGA IDE and arbitrary project import/editing.
- Full Verilog/SystemVerilog compatibility, DPI/external C++/arbitrary filesystem access, and physical FPGA synthesis or programming.
- SNES or other large RTL demonstrations.
- Custom Rust replacements for Verilator, Yosys, or the C++ toolchain.
- A public remote compilation backend.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh static site served under `/webrtl/` loads all browser-compile tooling and runtime assets without a compilation server.
- [ ] A user edits the provided counter RTL, clicks Compile, and the browser compiles the **edited HDL** and instantiates its newly generated simulation.
- [ ] With the original counter, Reset yields 0 and Step increments modulo 256; with a changed increment such as `8'd3`, Step yields 3 then 6. The results come from the newly compiled RTL circuit.
- [ ] Run, Pause, Step and Reset work after compiling and recompiling. Recompilation safely discards/pauses the previous model.
- [ ] Invalid RTL reports actionable compiler errors in the UI without breaking subsequent attempts.
- [ ] The compilation is asynchronous/non-blocking for the UI; the site remains responsive, with a visible compiling state.
- [ ] The published static-site build and documented local preview do not require the trusted-local Python build service for users' HDL edits. The existing local development flow remains functional unless a focused replacement is explicitly justified.
- [ ] Automated/reproducible browser tests verify real client-side RTL compilation, execution, edit/recompile behavior, failure recovery, and serving at the GitHub Pages subpath.
- [ ] Browser/toolchain compatibility, size/time/memory limits, and unsupported RTL features are documented; generated HDL and build artifacts do not get uploaded to a remote service.

## Optional validation

- Benchmark in-browser compile time, downloaded toolchain size, peak memory, and simulation cycles/second.
- Prototype a two-module design and record remaining work for multi-file/top-module support.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, verify the published GitHub Pages site can compile edited RTL and run it. This live deployment check is separate from pre-merge acceptance.

## Related

- #3 — Project vision
- #4 — Initial local browser simulation MVP
- #6 — Static GitHub Pages counter demo
